frontMatter.title: Phase 08 evidence: Web, Lite, SSH, headless and TUI control (remote/host matrix)

summary: Phase 08 bound the non-desktop surfaces to the managed admission built in phases 06 and 07, on feature/mega-maestro-v1.1.0-rc in the Maestro checkout (macOS, Darwin 27, Node v26.12.0). Which transport admitted a web-server caller (a Web Login cookie, the CLI per-boot secret, a Lite pairing, the bare path token) is resolved once per dispatch and bound at the host's sinks as attribution, never as tenant IAM: the renderer round trip carries a host-minted single-use dispatch ticket for send_command, cross_agent_ask, new_ai_tab_with_prompt, enqueue_command and open_terminal_tab, the web PTY and the desktop terminal tab record the actor they were admitted for and bind relayed writes to it under management, every dispatch reauthorizes against the socket's current standing so a revoked or unauthorized socket issues nothing, and a paired device is refused as unauthenticated until a registered enterprise actor exists while its pairing credential has one home and never leaves the machine. An SSH remote under management is qualified by the enrolled remote runtime's own attestation (maestro-cli host status --json read through readRemoteAttestation and judged by sshRemoteEndpointProblems, which requires the same tenant and org, a registered authority, a policy no older than ours and the REMOTE's own route table confining the provider's SSH arrivals), never by a working login or a local approval; the desktop sink qualifies before any side effect, the lease target names the remote endpoint, the ssh child is admitted only on it, and an unresolved or unqualified remote fails with nothing run on either machine. The headless host attests its standing in host status, composes its custody when a protected seal exists and otherwise names the missing seal; a detached host answers bounded managed operations over the WebSocket bridge in its own scope with single-writer and policy-generation checks, and the facade records the admitting transport. Deterministic coverage over the real handler chain, the real pairing registry, the real spawn authority, the real resolver, wrapper and launch plan, and the real runtime server and client is green (40 focused files, 2005 tests). The real paired host/client run below is REAL and not mocked: the built maestro-cli host and the built library drove managed operations across processes over the per-boot secret, and every scope, principal, installation, delegation, policy-revision and forged-secret refusal held. It is also standalone: no protected seal exists off Electron and no enrollment exists anywhere (CP-04), so no managed standing was attested, the real remote probe reading is unattested, and this build's own attestation is refused on its ssh row because SSH arrivals are not confined by any provider in this build. Transport authentication is recorded as admission; it is never counted as confinement, and no acceptance row that needs enrollment or confinement is counted as passed. The labeled container run of the real sibling endpoint with the 0.16.0 library at this HEAD is recorded as failed-attempt evidence.

realHostClientRun.reading: The bridge contract of MRC-08-05/05A holds across real processes: the per-boot secret admits a caller, the scope it reads is the host's own, the facade records host-secret as the admitting transport, and a caller cannot name its transport, act as another principal, name another installation or epoch, carry a delegation, or submit on a policy generation the host does not apply; a forged secret is turned away at the upgrade. None of that is confinement: the host is standalone and unenrolled, so no lease, policy or remote confinement was exercised, and the attestation a remote running this build would present is refused by the rule on its own ssh row. Nothing here counts transport authentication as enforcement.

deterministicCoverage.doubles: The renderer (a fake renderer callback in messageHandlers.test.ts), the process spawn port's lease authority (fakeSpawnPort in device-credentials.test.ts), the in-memory custody view and a registered ManagedEnrollmentStatus (remote.test.ts, server.test.ts and the live round trip), the in-repo fake endpoint daemon (host-adapter and runtime tests), ssh itself (buildSshCommand mocked in remote.test.ts). Everything else is real: resolveTransportAdmission, transportSpawnActor, the dispatch ticket registry, createProcessSpawnAuthority with one verifier per peer, the PairedDevices registry over real files, redactSecrets, ProcessManager.admitSpawn and buildSpawnRequestSnapshot, ChildProcessSpawner.managedChildRefusal, resolveSshLaunchTarget, qualifySshLaunchTarget, wrapManagedSpawnWithSsh, buildAgentLaunchPlan, readRemoteAttestation, createRemoteEndpointQualifier, hostManagedStanding, composeHostManaged, startRuntimeServer and createWsMaestroClient over a real socket, runtime turns over a fake agent child process.
cases: Transport admission (transport-actor, bridgeHandlers, messageHandlers, web-server-factory, wsRoute): a Web Login cookie, the CLI per-boot secret, a Lite pairing and the bare path token resolve to distinct admissions once per dispatch; the web PTY spawn is admitted for that actor instead of refused blind; remote credential mutation stays rejected; force reaches the renderer's busy guard and never the policy

Sink-side actors (spawn-authority, currentSpawnActor, handle-spawn, serveSpawn): host-secret and device-pairing join web-login and in-process; one verifier per peer, the record exhaustive; the chain records the transport (human web-login:<user>, service maestro-cli, service lite-device:<id>) while the principal stays the enrollment's registered actor; a CLI caller is no longer the desktop operator and a paired device no longer a Web Login human; standalone unchanged

Dispatch tickets (transport-actor, currentSpawnActor, messageHandlers, useRemoteIntegration, useRemoteHandlers, agentStore, queuedPrompt, cross-agent, consult-runner, crossAgentAsk, useCrossAgentDispatch, terminalSpawn, terminalTabHelpers, process.ts): issued inside the client context, single use, bound to agent and tab, expire on the injected clock, evicted past the cap, withdrawn on refusal or throw; an unknown, spent, expired, mismatched or forged ticket binds the caller's own standing (in-process), never the ticket's claim; carried on the spawn config and the QueuedItem, never the resilience snapshot; the consult route claims at cross-agent:send; the desktop terminal tab claims at process:spawnTerminalTab and records its actor for write_terminal_tab

Reauthorization and revocation (messageHandlers, WebSocketMessageHandler, terminalCallbacks, CallbackRegistry): every dispatch and terminal write checks isAuthorized() first; a revoked socket fans nine message kinds into no callback, no ticket and no reply; a device dropped a message ago is refused the next; a reconnecting device is the same actor with a ticket of its own; subscription or read access is never effect authority

Identity across surfaces (MRC-08-06, messageHandlers): acting-user mismatch (alice and bob to one agent bind two actors sameSpawnActor tells apart; a CLI socket with a cookie is attributed to the account in History but its ticket binds host-secret; an account named like a device is a web-login, not the device)

Lite separation (device-credentials, litePairingCredential, redactSecrets, cue-bundle-exporter, spawn-authority): a resolved device is { kind: lite, deviceId: <public half> } then { peer: device-pairing }, refused unauthenticated by name until a registered actor exists, then admitted as that actor with lite-device:<id> on the chain; the proof and the credential appear nowhere in admission, actor, chain or verified context; a pasted credential is redacted; both pairing store files are refused from a Cue bundle; a restarted registry resolves the same credential to the same actor; revoke leaves nothing live or after restart while another device still resolves only at its own instance and origin

Remote endpoint identity (ssh-remote-resolver, ssh-spawn-wrapper, remote, launch-plan): the reading is unreachable, unattested or attested-unread; the rule checks shape, then same tenant and org, registered authority, policy not behind, and the provider's ssh row on the REMOTE's table; a working login or a local approval proves nothing; an unresolved or unqualified remote refuses with nothing run on either machine and never a local fallback; the wrapper never degrades to local; the expectation comes from the sealed enrollment and refuses with none; the probe runs the launch's own ssh command for maestro-cli host status --json, bounded in time and bytes; under management every unresolved case keeps the resolver's reason; an approved credential on a remote is managed-credential-remote with the sentinel nowhere

The sink (handle-spawn, process.test.ts, serveSpawn, ChildProcessSpawner): with standing managed and SSH on, remote.qualify runs beside the launch plan before any side effect; a refusal is reported through reportSpawnRefusal with no pid; the qualified identity rides ProcessConfig.sshRemoteEndpoint, the lease target names the remote installation and authority (digest changes with it), and managedChildRefusal admits the ssh route only while the endpoint is bound; the local ssh row is never consulted for ssh; CLI and Cue keep refusing managed SSH at the plan

The headless host (server, runtime-host, host, host-managed): HostStatusReport.managed from the host's own custody, policy and lifecycle only (none on standalone or a non-ok view; authority registered only while registered; routes = the ssh row per visible provider); composeHostManaged over a protected seal composes identity store, endpoint client, lifecycle and host adapter and attaches only on an ok record, or refuses by name (seal first, keyring never consulted without one); managedUnavailable in the report and the Managed: line; the real host above reports exactly that

The bridge (server-requests, ws-client, server, turns, operations, index): managed_operation answered in the runtime's scope; installation, runtime and epoch must all match; the actor must be the scope's with an empty delegation; submit, cancel and interrupt need the host's policy revision; inputs shaped per operation; a caller-named peer refused invalid-input; the facade verifies with the transport's verifier (host-secret:<runtimeId>) and refuses a transport it has no verifier for; the in-process facade still reads in-process; the turn service fences before a spawn and refuses a managed turn that brought no lease (terminated, journaled failed, managed-unavailable); an unmanaged send on an enrolled headless runtime stays unmanaged by the phase 02 rule
